## Summary
- Give the hosted llvmpipe run 120 seconds to collect 60 frames per quick-matrix cell, leaving 45 post-warmup samples.
- Reject any head or baseline cell without a positive parsed frame measurement as an infrastructure error, and verify that the PR wrapper propagates the error without posting a verdict.
- Upload the complete perf run, including per-cell logs, for seven days so measurement failures are diagnosable from the workflow run.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 scripts/perf/tests/test_baseline_layouts.py` — all arms passed, including the new report-less head arm.
- [x] `bash scripts/perf/tests/test_baseline_writer.sh` — all 32 writer and reader assertions passed.
- [x] `bash test/tools/normalization_test.sh` — 16 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] `ruff check scripts/` — all checks passed.
- [x] `bash scripts/fleet/tests/test_workflow_paths_sync.sh` — 25 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] `python3 scripts/lint_comment_refs.py` — none above budget.
- [x] `fleet-build --target IRPerfGrid` — built target IRPerfGrid.
- [x] `fleet-pr-overlap --base master --repo engine` — `VERDICT: clean`.
- [x] Report-less matrix control with a failing `fleet-run` stub — the matrix exited 1 with `2/2 cell(s) produced no profile report`.
- [x] Perf Gate runs [35252756484](https://github.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/actions/runs/35252756484) and [35252805264](https://github.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/actions/runs/35252805264) — diagnostics uploaded; both cells recorded `exit_status: 134`, `status: no_report` after the hosted OpenGL compiler rejected `any(bool)`.

## Acceptance evidence
| Criterion | Check run | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| A report-less head run is an infrastructure error and produces no PR verdict | `python3 scripts/perf/tests/test_baseline_layouts.py` arm H | Checker and wrapper both exited 2; no `gh` comment invocation was recorded; the missing measurement reached stderr. |
| The hosted runner gets a bounded quick-matrix window and retains diagnostics | Runs 35252756484 and 35252805264 | The two-cell matrix returned in 10–11 seconds and uploaded both cell logs plus the manifest. It did not measure: both cells abort in shader compilation with exit 134. |
| Existing layout, exit mapping, branch writer, and normalization behavior remains intact | Layout, writer, and normalization controls listed above | All controls passed locally: layout/exit arms, 32 writer assertions, and 16 normalization assertions. |
| A push or dispatch cannot persist a report-less run | Failing `fleet-run` matrix control | Matrix exited 1 after writing diagnostics; commit `12e8918a7` moves this failure before the baseline writer. |

## Notes for reviewer
This is the measurement-layer remainder discovered while PR #2997 completed the reader and writer work. The uploaded logs corrected the earlier timeout diagnosis: Mesa rejects `any(ivec2(...) != ...)` from `c_voxel_to_trixel_stage_1_body.glsl`, so the process aborts before frame 1. Resolving that shader-compilation defect crosses the opus worker's render boundary; issue #2817 is retagged fable and this PR remains WIP with `Refs` until the final red-path proof can run.

Refs #2817

Authored by Codex (GPT-5 runtime).

## Summary
- `fleet-clip` accepts a literal `-` in the `<before>` position and writes a single-pane `<out-basename>.mp4`/`.gif` carrying only the "after" label overlay — for a PR with no before capture (a new demo, or the PR that adds `--auto-record` itself). `-` in the `<after>` position is a usage error (exit 2, one stderr line, no output).
- `fleet-clip` creates the parent directory of `<out-basename>` before composing, so a standalone compose no longer needs a manual `mkdir -p`.
- The two-arm path (`filter_complex` string, input order, encoder flags, GIF filter) is byte-for-byte unchanged — proven by an exact md5 match against master's script on identical synthetic inputs.
- `docs/agents/skills/attach-screenshots.md` documents the single-arm form (steps 5, 7) and notes the Clip markdown line is unchanged either way (step 8); `fleet-help`'s usage entry and the script's docstring both updated to match.
- Registers `scripts/fleet/fleet-clip` in `ruff.toml`'s `extend-include` — the row #3493 omitted, which is what has `fleet-tests.yml` red on master today via `test_lint_python_registry.py`.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash scripts/fleet/tests/run_all.sh --only fleet_clip` → `PASS test_fleet_clip.sh` (26 assertions: paired-mode regression, single-arm positive-fire label check, mkdir-creates-directory, missing-input/missing-ffmpeg/dash-in-after negative controls).
- [x] `bash scripts/fleet/tests/run_all.sh` on the PR head → 190 suites, 189 passed, 1 failed (`test_cross_repo_shared_file_parity.sh`, pre-existing on master at the PR's base commit `348d40bd1`, unrelated `classify-auto-rereview.sh` drift against the downstream game repo).
- [x] Same run on unmodified master at `348d40bd1` → 190 suites, 188 passed, 2 failed (`test_cross_repo_shared_file_parity.sh` and `test_lint_python_registry.py`). The PR's failed set is exactly master's minus `test_lint_python_registry.py`.
- [x] `python3 scripts/fleet/tests/test_lint_python_registry.py` → 18/18 pass on the PR head (fails on unmodified master, naming `fleet-clip`).
- [x] `ruff check --config ruff.toml scripts/fleet/fleet-clip` → `All checks passed!`.
- [x] Two-arm byte-identity A/B: staged master's `fleet-clip` + both label PNGs in a scratch dir, ran it and the PR's script against the same 320x180 `testsrc`/`testsrc2` inputs — both `out.mp4` are 40675 bytes, md5 `01b445993a2d58d7d1068f2353e2197b`.
- [x] `fleet-validate-roles` → `attach-screenshots.md (12 keys)` PASS for `[engine] SKILL.md` (no new delta key introduced).
- [x] `./scripts/fleet/fleet-help | grep -A2 fleet-clip` shows the `<before.mp4>|-` usage form.

| Criterion | Check run | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Single-arm output (positive-fire) | `bash scripts/fleet/tests/run_all.sh --only fleet_clip` | `PASS test_fleet_clip.sh`; single-arm `out-single.mp4` is 320x180 (the input's own size), `out-single.gif` present; label-crop mean luma 37.47 (fires > 20), control-crop mean luma 0.0 (< 5) |

Two-arm regression, exact | md5 A/B against `git show origin/master:scripts/fleet/fleet-clip` on identical `testsrc`/`testsrc2` inputs | both `out.mp4` = 40675 bytes, md5 `01b445993a2d58d7d1068f2353e2197b`; `git diff origin/master -- scripts/fleet/fleet-clip` shows no hunk inside `compose_mp4`'s `filter_complex` or `compose_gif`'s `vf` string |

`fleet-pr-overlap --base master` reports a non-blocking overlap: `#3507 scripts/fleet/fleet-help clean` — #3507 touches unrelated campaign-seeding entries in the same file, not the `fleet-clip` usage line this PR edits.

## Summary
- Define `UNICODE` for RtAudio's `rtaudio` target on Apple builds only, so its CoreAudio device-enumeration path takes the UTF-8 branch (`kCFStringEncodingUTF8`) instead of `CFStringGetSystemEncoding()` (MacRoman).
- Without this, a CoreAudio device name containing a curly apostrophe encodes as a single MacRoman high byte (`0xD5`) in the logged `Device: ` line, which makes the whole run log fail UTF-8 validation and makes the harness's `ugrep -I` (skip-binary) match nothing for every pattern on that file.

## Test plan
- [x] `cmake --preset macos-debug` + `fleet-build --target IRLuaWidgetsDemo` — clean build, rtaudio recompiles with the new define.
- [x] `fleet-run IRLuaWidgetsDemo --auto-screenshot 5 > /tmp/run.log 2>&1` then `file /tmp/run.log` — now `Unicode text, UTF-8 text` (was `ISO-8859 text`).
- [x] `fleet-build --target IRShapeDebug` + `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-screenshot 3` — `RESULT=CLEAN` (re-run after the `IR_isDarwin` amend; `flags.make` still carries `-DUNICODE` ×1).
- [x] `linux-build` (Engine Tests) green on the amended head — run 35312216680.

## Acceptance evidence
| Criterion | Check run | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Build artefact carries `-DUNICODE` | `command grep -c -- '-DUNICODE' build/_deps/rtaudio-build/CMakeFiles/rtaudio.dir/flags.make` | `1` |
| Run log is valid UTF-8 | `iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 /tmp/run.log > /dev/null; file /tmp/run.log` | `iconv` exit 0; `file` reports `Unicode text, UTF-8 text` (no `ISO-8859`) |
| Positive-fire: device line still present, now UTF-8-encoded, harness grep matches command grep | `command grep -c 'Device: ' /tmp/run.log` → `3`; `perl -ne 'print if /\xE2\x80\x99/' /tmp/run.log \| command grep -c 'Device: '` → `1`; `grep -c EngineLog /tmp/run.log` vs `command grep -c EngineLog /tmp/run.log` | both `288` (harness grep and command grep now agree) |
| Other hosts unaffected | `if(IR_isDarwin)` guards the new `target_compile_definitions` call, so the generated flags for Linux/Windows builds are byte-for-byte unchanged. The only host CI job in this repo is `linux-build` (`.github/workflows/engine-tests.yml`); Windows has no GitHub job and is covered by the fleet's native-host smoke lane (`fleet:needs-windows-smoke`) after merge | structurally a no-op off Apple; `linux-build` green on the amended head `307828916`: https://github.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/actions/runs/35312216680 (Configure / Build tests / Run tests / Build smoke target all `success`) |
| macOS smoke still clean | `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-screenshot 3` | `ir-run: RESULT=CLEAN exe=IRShapeDebug exit=0` |
| Comment names the cause | `engine/audio/CMakeLists.txt` new comment | cites CoreAudio/`CFStringGetSystemEncoding()`/MacRoman without a stray-macro risk |

## Notes for reviewer
The one-shot `MB_CUR_MAX`/`AudioDeviceID ids[nDevices]` Clang VLA-extension warnings during the rtaudio rebuild are pre-existing upstream code, unrelated to this change (no `-Werror` on that target).

Closes #3514

## Summary
- `VideoManager::configureCaptureOutputResolution` accepts exactly one non-zero dimension (previously any single non-zero value reset both overrides to 0, with a warning); the setter now only clamps negatives to 0 and stores the rest as given.
- At recording start, `toggleCapture` resolves the pair via the new pure `IRVideo::resolveCaptureOutputResolution` (`engine/video/include/irreden/video/ir_video_types.hpp`): both unset follows the render output unrounded (byte-identical to today's OFF path); any set dimension, and any derived one, rounds down to even for yuv420p and floors at 2 so a degenerate override never hands the encoder a zero-sized dimension. The bitrate area-scaling gate widens from "both set" to "either set" and follows the resolved pair.
- `scripts/fleet/clip-preset.lua` now sets `video_capture_output_width` only, dropping the hard-coded `video_capture_output_height = 360` that pinned every clip to 16:9.
- New pure-function unit test `test/video/capture_output_resolution_test.cpp` (`CaptureOutputResolutionTest`, 8 tests + `static_assert`s) covers the full branch table: both-unset, both-set (+odd rounding), width-only, height-only, odd-quotient rounding, negative-as-unset, the floor-of-2 safety net on both the set and derived axis, and an unreported (0×0 or single-zero) render pair.
- A render pair with a dimension `< 1` — `RenderManager::m_viewport` is 0×0 until the window reports its first size and while minimized, and `toggleCapture`'s viewport fallback does not re-check it — has no aspect: the resolver treats it as square (the derived axis mirrors the set one) instead of dividing by zero, and `toggleCapture` skips the pixel-area bitrate scaling when the render area is zero rather than casting an infinite ratio to `int`.

## Test plan
- [x] `fleet-run IrredenEngineTest --gtest_brief=1` — full suite green (1823 passed, 1 pre-existing skip).
- [x] `fleet-run IrredenEngineTest --gtest_filter='CaptureOutputResolutionTest.*'` — 8/8 pass.
- [x] Zero render pair (scratch build with `outputResolution = ivec2(0)` forced after the viewport fallback in `toggleCapture`, then reverted and rebuilt; `strings` on the shipped binary confirms no residue): `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60 --config-preset <abs path>/scripts/fleet/clip-preset.lua` → log `Recording: source=1280x720 -> output=640x640 @ 1500000 bps`, `ffprobe` `640,640`, `RESULT=CLEAN` — no divide-by-zero, unscaled budget.
- [x] `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60 --config-preset scripts/fleet/clip-preset.lua` (16:9, 1280x720 source) → log `Recording: source=1280x720 -> output=640x360 @ 375000 bps`; `ffprobe` confirms `capture.mp4` is 640x360.
- [x] `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60` (no preset, both-zero path) → log `Recording: source=1280x720 -> output=1280x720 @ 10000000 bps` (unscaled default bitrate); `ffprobe` confirms 1280x720.
- [x] `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60 --config-preset <preset overlaying game_resolution_width=800, game_resolution_height=600, video_capture_output_width=640, video_capture_bitrate=1500000>` (non-16:9, 4:3 render) → log `Recording: source=800x600 -> output=640x480 @ 960000 bps`; `ffprobe` confirms 640x480 (H/640 = 0.75, matching the 800x600 source aspect exactly).
- [x] `git grep -n 'needs both dimensions' -- engine/video` → 0 hits (the retired warning).
- [x] `fleet-build --target format-changed` clean.

## Acceptance evidence
| Criterion | Check run | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (no GPU): `CaptureOutputResolutionTest.*` passes, full binary green | `fleet-run IrredenEngineTest --gtest_filter='CaptureOutputResolutionTest.*'` then full suite | 8/8 pass; full suite 1823 passed / 1 pre-existing skip |
| Zero render pair does not divide by zero (review needs-fix) | scratch build forcing the render pair to 0×0 in `toggleCapture`, `--auto-record 60` under `clip-preset.lua` + `ffprobe`; plus the 4 `static_assert` rows / runtime test for 0×0, 0×720, 1280×0 | log: `source=1280x720 -> output=640x640 @ 1500000 bps`; ffprobe: `640,640`; `RESULT=CLEAN` |
| 16:9 non-regression (live) | `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60 --config-preset scripts/fleet/clip-preset.lua` + `ffprobe` | log: `source=1280x720 -> output=640x360 @ 375000 bps`; ffprobe: `640,360` — matches the plan's measured baseline exactly |
| Non-16:9 (positive-fire, live) | `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60 --config-preset <800x600 game_resolution + width=640>` + `ffprobe` | log: `source=800x600 -> output=640x480 @ 960000 bps`; ffprobe: `640,480` — matches the plan's predicted delta exactly (today's behavior on this preset was `output=800x600 @ 1500000 bps`) |
| Both-zero unchanged (live) | `fleet-run IRShapeDebug --auto-record 60` (no preset) | log: `source=1280x720 -> output=1280x720 @ 10000000 bps`; ffprobe: `1280,720` — no bitrate scaling on the OFF path |
| Warning retired | `git grep -n 'needs both dimensions' -- engine/video` | 0 hits |
| Format | `fleet-build --target format-changed` | `Built target format-changed`, no diffs after |

Host: macOS (Metal), `IRShapeDebug` built at this branch's head.

## Notes for reviewer
- The first commit on this branch missed the issue's `## Plan` comment (only the issue body was read) and diverged on the resolver's contract — a different function name, and even-rounding done in the setter instead of the resolver, with no floor-of-2 safety net. The second commit reconciles the implementation, tests, and docs with the plan (and its `## Plan corrections` amendment) verbatim; the live evidence above matches the plan's predicted numbers exactly.
- `fleet-pr-body-lint 3511` reads `ERROR #3511: issue #3511 plan: mixed prose and list acceptance criteria` (exit 2). Root cause: the plan's `### Acceptance criteria` list is followed by a trailing sentence ("Height-only is proven by the unit rows…") before the next heading — the same trailing-paragraph shape #3428 explicitly left unfixed ("The parser's rule is right to refuse a paragraph *after* an item… a `## Plan corrections` comment does not rescue the parse" — #3428's last comment, precedent on #3162 → PR #3442). Evidence rows above are hand-verified against the plan's own criteria 1–6 instead.

Closes #3511

## Summary
- `ir-build` now retries once on a build failure when CMake's own `cmake_check_build_system` check regenerated the tree — the case where `--target` names a target added since the build dir's last configure (a branch switch that `add_subdirectory`s a new demo).
- Mechanism: run the build as today; only on failure, run the check directly (bare, outside the CPU lock); if its combined output contains `Build files have been written to`, print one announce line and retry the build once; otherwise (or if the check itself fails) exit with the original/check status unchanged. Success path is byte-identical to before — zero added latency.
- Two new `scripts/fleet/tests/` suites: `test_ir_build_stale_target_retry.sh` (hermetic stub-cmake truth table, 7 arms) and `test_ir_build_stale_target_real_cmake.sh` (real cmake+make against a `project(probe NONE)` fixture).

## Summary
- `fleet-up` reads `FLEET_CAMPAIGNS` (space- or comma-separated objective slugs) from `~/.fleet/fleet-up.conf`. For each slug it ensures `.claude/worktrees/campaign-<slug>` off `origin/master`, writes the standard worktree settings (edit guard, session-track hook, auto permission mode), and babysits a persistent fable pane in a third tmux window, `campaigns`, launched as `campaign-<slug>`. A malformed slug or one with no `docs/design/campaigns/<slug>.md` on the clone is skipped with a warning, so a typo never opens an empty pane. Campaign worktrees are never reset at boot; the role resumes its own slice branch.
- `fleet-babysit` maps a `campaign-<slug>` role to `/role-campaign <slug> <mode>` (the shared wrapper takes the slug as its argument), treats it as resume-eligible like the architects (own `~/.fleet/sessions/campaign-<slug>.session-id`, `--resume` with no prompt on relaunch, dead-pointer fallback), and exports the session-track gate as `role=campaign mode="<slug> <mode>"` so a `/clear` re-injects `role-campaign.md` with its arguments.
- `fleet-down` treats `campaign-*` panes like architects (interactive, reachable for the shutdown summary).
- Conf sample block, `fleet-help` (index entry and per-tool summary), `scripts/fleet/README.md`, the campaign protocol's **launcher** delta and the engine wrapper now name the config path as the scheduled way to start a campaign; `solo-architect --campaign` stays the by-hand way.
- No scout, dispatcher or claim changes: a campaign pane carries no `@fleet-role` tag and never receives dispatched work.

## Test plan
- [x] `scripts/fleet/tests/run_all.sh --only babysit` → 3 suites PASS, including new T8 (campaign first launch fires `/role-campaign million-entity-render live`, persists its own sidecar, exports `role=campaign mode=million-entity-render live`) and T9 (campaign resume is `--resume <id>` with no prompt)
